doc.title: Nat Hentoff interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007

title: Whether jazz affects his writing
summary: He writes like a conversation, following Murray Kempton, who wrote for Jo Jones among others.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Does that kind of — how do I say this — does jazz effect the way you write?

Well the way I write is — Murray Kempton who was a reporter/columnist who I learned a lot from, he used to say he wrote for two or three people, like a conversation. One of them was Jo Jones. And I don’t conceptually, but I write like a conversation. I write as if I were talking to somebody. And in that respect I suppose growing up on the conversation that is jazz may have. I don’t know that it ever did in any kind of intellectual sense.
